transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net technical support. My name is Alex. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Alex. I've got a major problem with the wireless internet reaching my detached garden office at the back of the house.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can certainly help investigate that wireless coverage issue for you, Kieran. Before we begin, could you please confirm your full postal address and the security question answer for account verification?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it's 52 Richmond Vale, Bristol, BS8 2HY. And the security question is my favorite pet, which is Barnaby.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Kieran, that matches our system records. What is currently happening when you try to connect from the garden office?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I work as a self-employed architectural designer, and the connection has completely dropped out this morning! I've lost four hours of billable project time, and my client has threatened to cancel my contract and fine me two thousand pounds if the planning drawings aren't uploaded by five PM! I am tearing my hair out!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let's check the router details. What model of S-Net Hub do you have located in the main house?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's the Hub 4 with the circular silver base.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And how far away in meters is the garden office from the back wall of the house?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's roughly eighteen meters across the lawn and patio.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So if I have understood correctly, your workstation in the detached garden office cannot maintain a stable signal over the eighteen-meter distance through patio glass, causing your drawing uploads to fail. Is that right?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, exactly. It connects for thirty seconds, then drops completely, showing no internet secured.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously high-frequency 5 gigahertz radio waves suffer severe signal attenuation when traveling through modern energy-efficient argon double glazing, Kieran. But 2.4 gigahertz waves penetrate obstacles far more effectively.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, so how do I force my computer to use the 2.4 gigahertz signal?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: By default, the Hub 4 combines both frequencies into a single network name. We need to log into the router settings and split the frequencies into separate network names so your office devices can connect exclusively to the longer-range frequency.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, I can do that. What address do I type in?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Open a web browser on a laptop in the main house and type 192.168.1.1 into the address bar.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'm in the kitchen near the router now. Typing 192.168.1.1... the S-Net Hub login page has loaded.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: On the back of the Hub 4, there is a removable plastic settings card. It lists the Admin Password for the web interface.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Pulling out the card... the admin password is zebra-copper-92. Typing that in now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Once logged in, click on the Advanced Settings tab at the top, and select Wireless Configuration.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Clicking Advanced Settings... and Wireless Configuration.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You will see a checkbox labeled Synchronize 2.4GHz and 5GHz network names. Please uncheck that box.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Unchecking the box now... okay, two separate SSID fields appeared below.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: For the 2.4GHz SSID, append the letters -Garden to the existing network name, so it reads S-Net-WiFi-Garden.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Done, it now says S-Net-WiFi-Garden for the 2.4 band.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Keep the password identical so you don't have to remember two different keys, and then click Apply Changes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Clicking Apply Changes... the hub light is flashing green while it saves the split SSIDs.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: While it reboots the wireless radios, do you have an S-Net Wi-Fi Booster pod in the house?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, I have one that came in the box, but I had it plugged into the garden office itself.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Placing the booster in the dead zone itself is ineffective because the booster needs a strong signal to repeat. Move that booster into the rear kitchen window, halfway between the router and the garden office.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Ah, that makes total sense! I'm plugging the booster into the kitchen windowsill socket facing the garden right now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The booster LED will turn solid white when it synchronizes with the new split 2.4GHz garden network.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's pulsed white and now it's solid white. I'm walking down the garden path to the office with my laptop.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Take your time. Let me know when you reach your desk in the garden office.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'm at my desk in the garden studio now. Looking at available Wi-Fi networks... S-Net-WiFi-Garden has appeared with full five bars!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Connect to S-Net-WiFi-Garden using your standard Wi-Fi password.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Entering password... Connected, secured! Full signal bars.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to check, Kieran, is the signal indicator on your CAD workstation still showing four to five full bars without fluctuating?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Solid five bars, rock steady. Let me start uploading this architectural drawing package to the client FTP server.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Go ahead, let's observe the upload transfer speed and ensure it maintains continuous throughput without dropped packets.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The transfer bar is moving rapidly... upload speed is holding steady at forty-five megabits per second! The full project file just uploaded and sent!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's fantastic! Your file is uploaded well in advance of your five PM deadline.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Alex, you have saved my bacon today. That was forty-five megabits upload all the way down here at the bottom of the garden.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm delighted to hear that, Kieran. Splitting the bands and positioning the booster as a relay in the kitchen window ensures maximum penetration across the patio.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It worked like a charm. What about the wireless channel if neighbors in Bristol are broadcasting on the same frequency?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The Hub 4 includes automatic Dynamic Channel Allocation, so it continually monitors background noise and shifts between channels one, six, and eleven.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That explains why the signal is so stable right now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exactly. You won't have to adjust channels manually in the future.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can I also run an external Cat6 Ethernet cable out here in the future if I decide to trench the lawn?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, absolutely! The Hub 4 has four Gigabit Ethernet ports on the back, so you can run an outdoor armored cable directly into a desktop switch in your studio.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is definitely my long-term project for the spring.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That will give you full Gigabit wired speeds. But for today, your 2.4GHz garden wireless link is robust and performing brilliantly.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you so much for the clear technical guidance.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Did you also want to test connecting your tablet or phone to the new garden SSID as well while we are on the line?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me test my iPad here on the drafting table... connected immediately and browsing smoothly.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Splendid. Both your primary workstation and secondary mobile devices are now reliably connected on the dedicated garden band.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Everything is running like clockwork now. What a massive relief.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will remain the dedicated case owner for this ticket and log these Wi-Fi configuration adjustments so if you ever need further optimization, our team has full notes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's wonderful, thank you for making sure everything is recorded.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else regarding your broadband or WiFi coverage that I can check for you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, that has solved my crisis completely. Thanks again Alex.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net, Kieran. Have a successful afternoon and good luck with the architectural submission!

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks! Bye.
